channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Six new traditional Belgian restaurants awarded 'Brusselicious' label
item.description: The six new ones join the nearly 40 other restaurants in the Brussels-Capital Region that already hold the label.

item.title: Rats are thriving in Brussels. Can the city stop feeding them?
item.description: Brussels is stepping up its fight against rats with smart traps and a bigger pest-control budget, but they will be difficult to eradicate from the city completely.

item.title: Police seek suspects who held Saint-Gilles residents at gunpoint
item.description: Police are searching for three people who allegedly held residents at gunpoint and tied them up before stealing jewellery, money and a Rolex from a home in Saint-Gilles.

item.title: Brussels police officer admits to stealing €25,000 while searching house for drugs
item.description: A Brussels police officer is in custody after admitting to taking €25,000 in cash, during a search linked to a drug trafficking investigation.

item.title: Motorists confused by Dutch-only road signs on Brussels Ring Road
item.description: Belgium's language watchdog has backed a complaint against Dutch-only motorway signs around Brussels, raising questions about signage across the capital.

item.title: Energy prices surge in Belgium – time to switch contracts?
item.description: Energy prices are rising sharply in Belgium as geopolitical tensions and the return of seasonal demand put renewed pressure on consumers.

item.title: 'The solution is not in prison': The magistrate who helped rewrite Belgium's rules of crime and punishment
item.description: One of the minds behind Belgium's new Criminal Code explains why prison is not the answer to every crime, stating that justice ought to be restorative.

item.title: Dozens of African students left in limbo after Brussels IT school goes bankrupt
item.description: Dozens of African students who paid thousands of euros to study IT in Brussels have been left without degrees and with little hope of recovering their money after their school went bankrupt.

item.title: Saint-Gilles majority to submit motion for national response to organised crime
item.description: The news comes after a fresh wave of shootings and vehicle fires in the municipality.

item.title: Belgium takes major step in French McKinsey tax fraud probe
item.description: Belgian prosecutors have seized more than €65 million as part of an ongoing French investigation into suspected tax fraud involving consulting giant McKinsey.

item.title: Saint-Gilles snack bar fights closure over customers' alleged drug dealing
item.description: Sania snack bar manager said he cannot be held responsible for what customers do without his knowledge.

item.title: Brussels-West police seize more than €1 million and arrest 133 people this year
item.description: The Anti-Burglary Brigade (BAB) of the Brussels-West police zone has seized more than €1 million and arrested 133 people since the beginning of the year.

item.title: 'My dad is an ex-Jihadist': The first date stories you can't make up
item.description: At what point when you start dating someone should you reveal that you're related to a terrorist?

item.title: The crystal phoenix: 200 years of Val Saint Lambert
item.description: It is difficult to decide which is more impressive: the speed, the choreography or the sheer confidence of two glassblowers who make an extraordinarily difficult process look almost effortless.

item.title: Activists gather on Brussels street ot protest for climate action
item.description: Around 100 climate activists showed up near Brussels Central Station to urge policymakers to act against an impending environmental crisis.

item.title: Thousand-strong crowd expected to march for climate in Brussels
item.description: Over 1,000 people are expected to take to Brussels' streets to pressure Belgian and European authorities over climate policy.

item.title: Sheep parades still popular among Brussels residents
item.description: Eight retired ewes grazed the grass of Ixelles' public spaces for over a month as the municipality tries to reduce mechanical mowing.

item.title: Brussels struggles with managing surveillance camera system
item.description: Nearly a quarter of the region's surveillance cameras are out of service, while hundreds of unused devices are still sitting in storage.

item.title: Former Audi Brussels site to be transformed into business park with 3,000 jobs
item.description: Belgian property developer Heylen Warehouses has reached an agreement to acquire the former Audi Brussels site in Forest.

item.title: Jobseekers in Brussels are struggling to find roles – here's why
item.description: "Don't expect strong growth on the labour market in the short term," warns a senior economist following a new release of job seeker data for Brussels.
